clue.text: Magnificent problem —- turned out America's after power

indicators.note: after says the letters for power come in front of what follows, read in sequence

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem set in class
P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

indicators.note: turned means the little word out is flipped round to read backwards

parts.note: US is short for the United States, i.e. America

explanation.surface: A setback for America has followed some exercise of power, and it was a grand one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses the word out; 'after' says the reversed run and America come after the letter for power.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumptuous describes something lavish and splendid, a close synonym of magnificent.

clue.text: Drunkard clutches a bottle by the top, his sole support?

indicators.note: clutches means the drinker's letters hold the rest tightly inside them

parts.note: a sot is an old word for a habitual drinker; the run of letters across 'clutches a bottle' is a coincidence, since the container gives the same word

indicators.note: by the top asks for only the opening letter of the word bottle

explanation.surface: A drunk grips a bottle by its neck, and it is the only thing holding him up.
explanation.walkthrough: SOT goes round A plus B, the top of 'bottle'. The question mark flags a pun: a sabot is a wooden clog, literally supporting the sole of a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabot is a wooden shoe, so it supports the wearer's sole, a pun on 'only support'.

clue.text: "Eat no tat" — I'm Reine in revolution

definitions.text: "Eat no tat" — I'm Reine in revolution

indicators.note: in revolution says the letters are turned over and rearranged, like France turned upside down

explanation.surface: A French queen, speaking in a revolution, sniffily refuses to eat rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of EAT NO TAT IM REINE rearrange to the answer. The whole clue is the definition too: Reine is French for queen, and she fell in the French Revolution, famously (if apocryphally) saying 'let them eat cake'.
explanation.definitionFit: The doomed queen of France, executed in the Revolution, is pictured disdaining cheap food as a queen ('Reine').

clue.text: Girl travelling round a country — one in Africa

indicators.note: travelling round means the girl's name goes all the way around the other letters

explanation.surface: A young woman is touring a country, one on the African continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a country' looks as if it is the definition, but it is wordplay; the definition is 'one in Africa'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanzania is an East African nation, one of the countries on that continent.

clue.text: Squatter having to take place without food

explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of 'outside', not 'lacking'.
explanation.definitionFit: A squatter occupies a property, so is an occupier, though without any legal right.

clue.text: Succeeded getting very best funny man

explanation.walkthrough: The trailing W in the held text is an OCR stray from the page, not part of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A scream is informal for a hilarious person, so a comic or funny man.

explanation.definitionFit: A sentinel is a guard whose duty is to keep watch.

clue.text: Separate, from code to be deciphered, leading article in French
